name: Maldives
summary: A red field with a green rectangle in the centre bearing a white crescent. The plain red flag of the sultanate gained a green panel and crescent in the 20th century.
origin: The Maldives historically flew a plain red flag. In the early 20th century a black and white striped band (the dhandimathi) was added at the hoist, and a green panel with a crescent was added in the 1930s under Prime Minister Abdul Majeed Didi.
The striped hoist band was removed at independence from Britain on 26 July 1965.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The courage of the nation's heroes and their willingness to give their lives.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Peace and prosperity; also the coconut palms.

symbols.name: White crescent
symbols.description: A crescent in the green rectangle, opening toward the fly.
symbols.meaning: Islam, the religion of the state.

history.label: Sultanate
history.note: Plain red, later with a black and white hoist band, then a green panel and crescent.

facts: The Maldives is the lowest-lying country in the world.
It is also the smallest country in Asia by area.
The green panel is sometimes said to represent the coconut palm, essential to island life.
clues: A red field with a green rectangle containing a white crescent.
The flag of the world's lowest-lying country.
A black and white hoist band was removed at independence in 1965.
